mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation environment.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed NBER recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contracting manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the economy is in a deflationary regime.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.5% month-over-month indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of rising interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which precedes tighter monetary policy and higher wage inflation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days under a low-inflation regime.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 5% for six consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and services and supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous sharp rise in mortgage rates.
